default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-408.title: Five-minute candle-close painting fade
E-408.hypothesis: Many WIN chart traders and bots read 5-minute candles, so the final minute of each 5-minute block is where short-term players push the price to paint a breakout close; a 1-minute close through the recent box printed exactly in that minute is cosmetic demand, not a build-up of orders, and liquidity providers take it back once the new block opens, so fade it.

E-409.title: Yesterday's closing-hour range edge fade
E-409.hypothesis: The high and low of yesterday's last trading window bound where the closing flows (index funds, day-trade flattening, settlement hedgers) were matched; those participants rest orders at the edges the next day, so a bar that pokes beyond either edge and closes back inside meets that resting inventory, and price rotates back into the closing range; fade the poke.

E-410.title: Wide-CPR day micro-break fade
E-410.hypothesis: The central pivot range (pivot vs. high-low midpoint from yesterday) is wide when yesterday closed far from its middle; pivot traders read a wide CPR as a sideways day and quote both sides; on such days short-term box breaks hit passive traders who expect rotation, so the break fades back into the box.

E-411.title: Equity-specific day box-break follow
E-411.hypothesis: When the index's range so far is large next to the dollar's range (compared with the usual ratio at this minute), the day's moves come from equity-specific information, not FX flow; informed equity orders are split and persistent, so a box break on such a day has informed flow behind it; follow it.

E-412.title: Stalled-break fade
E-412.hypothesis: A close through the recent box followed at once by a bar that makes no further extreme and closes weaker, while still outside the box, shows the breakout buyers did not get any follow-through: the stops are used up and nobody new is paying up; the late breakout entrants exit before the box defenders even need to act, so fade the stall (before it fails back inside).

E-413.title: Lunch-anchored VWAP touch hold
E-413.hypothesis: The VWAP anchored at the B3 midday lull is the average cost of everyone who positioned for the afternoon (European close, US session flow); when price returns to it from one side and closes back on that side, that cohort defends its break-even, so trade away from the anchored level.

E-414.title: Away-from-yesterday day box-break follow
E-414.hypothesis: When little of today's range overlaps yesterday's range, the market has left yesterday's value and is looking for new participants (initiative, not responsive, trade); box breaks in the direction away from yesterday are with the initiative side, whose orders keep arriving, so follow only those breaks.

E-415.title: Dominant-volume bar side box-break follow
E-415.hypothesis: The bar with the most abnormal volume of the session so far (versus its time of day) marks where the day's largest participant acted, and its colour shows its side; that participant usually still has inventory to work, so box breaks in the same direction have it behind them; follow only those breaks.

E-416.title: Previous clock-hour extreme close-through fade
E-416.hypothesis: The high and low of the hour that just finished are the stops and breakout alerts of hourly-candle traders; when that hour was not unusually wide, the first close beyond its extreme is mostly those mechanical orders firing together, after which the hour's range players lean against it; fade the close.

E-417.title: Multi-day close-location giveback regime fade
E-417.hypothesis: When the last five sessions mostly closed near their lows, rallies have been sold into every day by holders using strength to reduce; that supply is still there, so an upward box break is sold into again and fades (mirror when sessions keep closing near their highs and dips are bought).
